title: Autumn 1 AP1 Assessment and Review
intro: A short, independent catch-up: learn the essential knowledge, practise and review answers.

questions.prompt: How can a larger cache help a CPU?
Which register holds the address of the next CPU instruction?
questions.feedback: The Program Counter stores the next instruction address.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the explanations, visual and model before answering.

blocks.title: Paper 1 knowledge
blocks.text: Review binary, character sets, image/sound file sizes, compression, RAM/ROM, storage and CPU architecture.

blocks.title: Paper 2 introduction
blocks.text: Review abstraction, decomposition, IPO, flowcharts, searching, simple sorting, variables and validation.

blocks.title: Show working
blocks.text: For calculations, write formula, substitute values, calculate bits and convert units. For algorithms, show intermediate steps.

blocks.title: Use feedback
blocks.text: Identify one concept you can explain clearly and one that requires further teaching or practice.

blocks.title: Visual model
blocks.caption: Use these linked concepts to explain your answer.

blocks.title: Worked example · Model a synoptic answer: calculate bitmap storage and explain a suitable device for a portable laptop.
blocks.text: A 50 × 40 bitmap at 8-bit colour depth has 50 × 40 = 2,000 pixels. Multiply by 8: 16,000 raw bits. Divide by 8: 2,000 bytes of uncompressed pixel data. For a laptop that may be knocked, select SSD for its lack of moving mechanical parts. State one drawback, such as higher cost per GB, and explain why this is not universal.

items: register — Small, fast CPU storage holding data or addresses.
compression — Reducing bits needed to represent a file.
validation — Checking data against specified input rules.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order.
items: Convert the bit total to bytes
answer: Convert the bit total to bytes
questions.feedback: Pixel count × colour depth gives bits; divide by eight for bytes.

questions.prompt: A 5 × 4 bitmap at 8 bits per pixel contains how many bytes of raw pixel data?
Linear search [2,5,6,1] for 6. What is its zero-based index?
questions.feedback: Index 0 is 2, index 1 is 5 and index 2 is 6.

questions.prompt: Width 10, height 5, depth 8: how many raw bits are printed?
If depth becomes 4, how many bits are printed?

writing.prompt: Explain abstraction and give an example of a detail that could be ignored in a storage-capacity calculator. [3 marks]
writing.model: Abstraction ignores unnecessary detail [1], while keeping essential information [1]; storage capacity and file size matter, device colour does not [1].

questions.feedback: That is the Program Counter's role.
